subject: Emotions
title: Surprise in Marketing
description: Learn Surprise in Marketing in one minute.

hook.text: Unboxing videos get billions of views. People watch strangers open packages for the surprise they feel vicariously.

buildup.text: Mystery boxes, blind bags, and loot crates all sell surprise itself. The product matters less than the reveal.

discovery.text: Variable reward schedules—the same principle behind slot machines—drive engagement in apps, games, and shopping.

twist.text: Belgium banned loot boxes as gambling. The surprise economy walks a thin line between delight and exploitation.

climax.text: Brands that deliver consistent small surprises build more loyalty than those with predictable rewards.

punchline.text: Marketers don't sell products. They sell the thrill of not knowing.

quiz.question: Why did Belgium ban loot boxes?
